must_find.description: An authenticated operator supplies workspace bay and an entry.name such as ../../outside.txt. Active binary/manifest/overlay reach shipping unpack -> decodeEntries (only string/length) -> materialize, where join normalizes parent segments and writeFile can overwrite process-writable files outside the selected workspace/root. No symlink or ZIP-library behavior is needed. State process filesystem permissions and operator credential prerequisites.

An authenticated operator can submit a single-line label containing command substitution, e.g. $(id), through active receipt route -> receiptLabel -> makeRenderRequest -> runRenderer. Label length/newline validation preserves shell syntax, and concatenating it within a double-quoted exec shell command permits commands with service-account authority. Program/output configuration is trusted; attacker needs only label control plus the operator credential. Distinguish this live sink from archived exec.

coverage.description: Resolve the binary entrypoint through the checked-in manifest, implementation and winning shipping overlay; the base compatibility router is not the shipped router.
Trace exact credential authentication followed by operator role enforcement; both findings require the shipping operator credential, not anonymous access.
Review the archive route, bounded entry decoding, service and final file path/write selection.
Review the receipt route, label validation, derived request and child process invocation as one chain; a single-line label can still contain shell syntax.
Assess body size, entry count/content limits and identifier constraints without claiming these limits provide path containment or process argument isolation.
